author: Codex (initial source review)
limitations: This is a complete raw-site review only for chainguard-dev/malcontent at the frozen 20-r2 pin. It does not establish coverage for other cohort members or complete P2.
Unresolved entries are not adopted contracts, eligible product questions, or outcome rows.

The exact replay requires the pinned YARA-X Go binding and native YARA-X C API 1.19.0 through pkg-config. The local replay build used those exact versions; the C API build recipe and product output are recorded in the adjacent author-Markdown calibration.

reviews.rationale: The interpolated names are escaped with regexp.QuoteMeta and come from static badRules/rulesWithWarnings maps. removeRules transforms YARA source before Recursive compiles it, and a cross-rule match could affect detection coverage. The CLI's current source is embedded rules plus optional thirdparty.FS, while the exported config can receive other filesystems. The attacker trust class and a product-level detection-integrity guarantee are not established here; keep pending a contract and exact YARA-X replay.

This pattern collapses runs of three or more newlines after selected rule blocks have been removed. It changes formatting in the transformed YARA source and has no independently evidenced security-boundary guarantee at this call site.
The pattern is local to a fuzz test that guards test inputs before calling the compiler. It is not on a product input-to-security-boundary path.

GetExt removes a trailing version suffix before archive-extension lookup. The path comes from the scan target, but this pattern performs filename normalization rather than an input validation or sanitization guarantee; archive extraction has separate content and path controls. No regex-specific security property is established by the inspected caller.
The pattern collapses repeated spaces in already rendered Markdown table text. It is a presentation cleanup operation, not the renderer's Markdown escaping control.
The pattern collapses repeated dashes in already rendered Markdown table text. It is a presentation cleanup operation, not the renderer's Markdown escaping control.

ansiLineLength removes matching codes only from a temporary string to calculate display width before truncation. The original content is still rendered, so this regex is not a terminal-output sanitizer.

Diff --report reads user-selected JSON/YAML reports; this pattern extracts conventional temporary-root prefixes, and CleanReportPath/FormatReportKey remove them before the diff report is rendered. The comments and examples support a possible local-path privacy contract, but the exact product-output property and end-to-end replay remain unverified.

review_refs.why: user-selected report loading and temporary-root extraction

reviews.rationale: This pattern extracts rule names in a unit-test helper over embedded third-party rules. It is not used by the product implementation.

The autonomous contract MC-malcontent-author-metadata-extra-markdown-link was adopted before its solver result and frozen in a one-question 20-r2 roster. The exact YARA-X-to-report.Generate-to-Markdown replay emitted a second attacker-chosen HTTPS link from valid rule metadata. This confirms the generated Markdown structure; downstream consumer impact and any upstream response remain pending.

reviews.rationale: dateRe is used to discard date-like tokens while generating third-party report keys. The observed behavior affects display naming and has no established security-boundary property in the inspected path.

This parser extracts rule declarations from rule source to build report/source-location indexing. It does not validate an untrusted input or sanitize a value for a security sink; correctness questions about source association would need a separate product requirement.
